pageCache.text:
A message for our Year 7 parents and carers:
Year 7 Meet the Tutor Evening.
This event provides an opportunity for you to meet your child's form tutor, who will be supporting them throughout the academic year. It is also a chance to find out how your child has settled into Year 7, learn more about life at The Portsmouth Academy, and ask any questions you may have about the year ahead.
To help keep all pupils safe, please ensure the school has up-to-date information about any allergies your child may have. Accurate allergy information enables us to put appropriate support plans in place, train staff effectively, and respond quickly in an emergency. We all have a part to play in creating a safe environment, including following our nut-aware policy and being mindful of the food brought into school. If your child has an allergy, please contact the school or update their details via Arbor. Be Allergy Aware Posters for AAW25
Welcome to The Portsmouth Academy
Empowering Young People to Meet the World
Welcome to The Portsmouth Academy. Our mission is to empower every pupil that comes to our school to meet the world with the knowledge and skills to prepare them for life.
Our work is build on a foundation of our three core values: Aspire, Achieve and Respect.
The Portsmouth Academy provides education to our students not just to support their academic progress, but to develop them into self-reflective learners with the knowledge and skills to become valuable members of any community.
Quick Links
Students and Parents
Term Dates
Our Values
Aspire
We work with students so that they are aspirational and ready for their next steps and, most importantly, understand their role and place both within their local community and beyond.
Achieve
The personal development of our students is vital for them to be able to reach their full potential. We know that successful people are able to both reflect on their strengths, and know the areas which they wish to develop in order to be successful in the next stage of their journey.
Respect
Respect for others, and respect for ourselves. This encompasses the school culture we seek to instill in our corridors and classrooms so that our young people are able to develop, personally and academically, in a considerate environment.
Latest News & Updates
Read more about the incredible achievements of our Year 11 students as we celebrated GCSE Results Day.
A team of our students won a debating competition, which saw them take on schools in Portsmouth and the surrounding area.
We loved hosting The Royal Institution here at The Portsmouth Academy, who put on an incredible STEM show for our students.
Will your child be starting secondary school in 2027? We'd love to welcome you to The Portsmouth Academy later this year to discover our wonderful school.

It was a day fuelled by fire, rockets and balloon-bursting at The Portsmouth Academy, as The Royal Institution dazzled our students and local community with a science show to remember.
There were two shows during the school day, one for Year 7 and one for Year 8, which focused on how viruses and diseases can spread.
In the afternoon, we hosted parents and children for a spectacular display on all things rockets and explosions.
The Royal Institution are an independent charity who bring the public and scientists together through engaging talks and initiatives.
Gareth Baston, who delivered the interactive sessions, loved the energy and enthusiasm shown by the pupils and their parents.
“It was great to be invited to The Portsmouth Academy and see the students so engaged with today’s topic.
“Their enthusiasm to take part in the demonstrations; their attentive listening and intelligent questions were really encouraging.
“Hopefully today’s sessions will inspire them to look towards STEM subjects and careers in the future”.
The shows provided a unique opportunity for students to bring their learning to life in an exciting, hands-on way.
Dara, one of our Year 7 pupils, enjoyed the element of surprise at the shows:
“It was very fun being here and all the cool tricks he did were so unexpected!”
Hosting our local community in the later show was a fantastic opportunity to show families how passionate we are about science here at The Portsmouth Academy.
One parent said, “This presentation will prepare the students to make their mind up about science in the future, because science is the future!”
Science, Technology, Engineering and Maths (STEM) are so important in helping our pupils aspire and achieve, by transforming their life chances and giving them an opportunity to pursue a career in the field.
Miss Steger-Lewis, STEM lead here at The Portsmouth Academy, recognised the importance of providing interactive experiences to ignite pupil’s passion for science.
“We were so fortunate to receive a grant from The Royal Institution as events like this are so important to our students.
“They bring what they learn in class to life and appreciate the real-world application of what they do in school. Families who attended really enjoyed the show too and it was lovely to share the experience with them”.
At The Portsmouth Academy, we help students fulfil their aspirations; providing opportunities for them to reach their full potential.
Does your child love science? Discover more about The Portsmouth Academy at our open day on Thursday 1st October 2026 from 6-8pm.

August 20, 2026 10:08am
Students and staff at The Portsmouth Academy, located on St Mary’s Road and part of Thinking Schools Academy Trust, are celebrating today as they receive their GCSE results.
School leaders say this results day, which are a record high over the last three years, reflects the hard work shown by students and the support given by both staff and families.
The number of students achieving a strong pass of grade 5 or higher in English and maths increased by 5%. The overall number of top grades also increased this year, with grades at 7 or higher rising by 3% and grades at 4 and 5 or higher increasing by 2%.
In addition, the school saw particular success in subjects including history, biology, chemistry and dance, where more than 20% of students achieved a grade 7 or higher.
Alongside the school's overall success, many students have achieved exceptional individual results, including:
Nakia Azad, who achieved a grade 9 in all of her GCSEs and passed both Level 2 Further Maths and Level 3 Algebra.
Josh Reid, who achieved a grade 9 in eight subjects and a grade 8 in another. He also passed both Level 2 Further Maths and Level 3 Algebra.
Maya Kopeky, who achieved four grade 9s, two grade 8s, two grade 7s and a Level 2 Distinction.
Julia Fariq, who achieved two grade 9s, six grade 8s and a grade 7.
Collecting his GCSE results today, Josh Reid, said:
“I’m so grateful to everyone that has supported me at TPA over the years. I am over the moon with my results.”
Sarah Dedman, Headteacher at The Portsmouth Academy, said:
“We are incredibly proud of our students, and the exam results they have achieved this year. These outcomes reflect the hard work, determination and resilience our young people have shown throughout their studies, and it is fantastic to see the improvements we have made continue to grow.
“These results are the product of a collective effort. I would like to thank our students for their commitment, our parents and carers for their unwavering support and our dedicated staff for the care, expertise and encouragement.
“We remain ambitious for every student and are excited about what lies ahead for them. We look forward to building on these successes and continuing to raise standards and opportunities for all young people at The Portsmouth Academy.”
Michelle Smith, Regional Director South at Thinking Schools Academy Trust, said:
“Congratulations to all students at The Portsmouth Academy on their fantastic achievements. These results reflect their hard work, alongside the dedication of staff and support of families. It is particularly pleasing to see the school achieve its strongest results in three years, demonstrating the continued progress being made across the Academy. We look forward to seeing what this talented cohort achieves next."

June 5, 2026 12:56pm
It is a privilege to be the Headteacher of The Portsmouth Academy and to play a part in the lives of the young people in our community.
As a long-standing leader at the school, I know our students and staff well. I am proud to build on the progress already made during my time as a senior leader at the school.
I am supported by an experienced leadership team, along with our Regional Director, Mrs Smith, and Mr Dolphin, Head of Standards and Assessment. Together, we will continue to support and challenge the school, so we keep improving.
I am working closely with leaders and schools across the Thinking Schools Academy Trust. By doing this, I can ensure the best practice is implemented in our school.
Starting secondary school is an important step. It brings excitement, curiosity, and new opportunities. At The Portsmouth Academy, we work hard to make sure every student feels known, valued, and supported from their very first day.
Our mission is simple: Transforming Life Chances. This guides everything we do and every decision we make.
We believe change happens through the “Thousand Little Moments” that take place every day. A friendly welcome at the door, extra help from a teacher, a new friendship forming, or a student trying something challenging, these small moments add up over time. Together, they build confidence, character, and ambition.
At The Portsmouth Academy, students try new subjects, take part in different opportunities, and make new friends. We encourage them to think carefully, work hard, and be kind to others. Our staff provide strong teaching and support so every student can succeed. We have high expectations because we believe every child can achieve their best.
We are proud of our community and the strong relationships we have with families and carers. By working together, celebrating success, and supporting each other through challenges, we help every student grow and succeed.
I would also like to thank our staff, students, and families for their continued hard work and support. Everything we do is focused on helping every child achieve the best possible outcomes, and we will keep working together to achieve this.
Thank you for placing your trust in us. Together, we will create the moments that shape the future.
Mrs S Dedman Headteacher, The Portsmouth Academy

Is your child looking to start secondary school in September 2027? We’d love to welcome you to The Portsmouth Academy for our Open Event on Thursday 1st October 2026, from 6-8pm.
We’re so excited to be opening our doors to Year 6 pupils and their families to see our wonderful school in action.
Alongside a welcome from our Headteacher Mrs S. Dedman, our current students at the school will be on hand to give tours, answer questions, and share what they love about the different subjects available.
There’ll also be the chance to try some free food on offer from our Food Technology department and see our range of modern facilities in action, such as our multi-use games area!
As a member of the Thinking Schools Academy Trust, we’re committed to Transforming the Life Chances of every pupil.
Our school encourages students to become self-reflective learners, and Mrs Dedman explains why thinking about our thinking is so important to our culture.
“We talk about education as being the golden ticket; the opportunity which opens up those next steps for young people after school.
“We’re a school committed to its values; to aspire and aim high, to achieve and get the very best out of themselves, and to show respect”.
Our ethos and values and our school motto: ‘Aspire, Achieve, Respect’, shape everything we do at The Portsmouth Academy.
Diversity is our strength and is embodied through We Are TPA, to celebrate our wonderful community of pupils, parents and staff.
Mrs Dedman discussed the student experience here at The Portsmouth Academy, which aims to enrich their learning in a variety of different ways.
“We want to make sure our pupils have a unique set of experiences during their time in school. Our curriculum is ambitious, broad, and provides pupils with the opportunity to study a range of different subjects.
“Alongside this, there’s also lots of extra-curricular activities and some exciting trips overseas”.
At The Portsmouth Academy, we strive to work closely with our families and parents to ensure every pupil receives the best possible experience.
At our Open Event, there’ll be plenty of opportunities to have an informal chat with our wonderful staff, who will be on hand to answer any questions you may have.
We recognise how daunting it can be for your child to start secondary school, and our Student Services team are proud to support every child with whatever they need to have a positive educational experience.
Fancy coming along to explore The Portsmouth Academy? You don’t need to pre-register; just turn up on the night!
Have any questions or require accessibility support to attend? Don’t hesitate to get in touch at info@theportsmouthacademy.org.uk

August 14, 2026 01:01pm
A team of our Year 7 and Year 9 students were recently crowned champions of The Big Debate 2026; a competition designed to challenge communication and presenting skills.
The event was run by UNLOC, an organisation which empowers young people to become changemakers. Facing competition from 13 other schools across the city, our students impressed with their performance and ability to think on their feet.
Without knowing which side they’d have to defend until the day itself, students discussed social media restrictions, renewable energy, and Portsmouth’s City of Culture bid, taking place later this decade.
This saw our students think critically about topics which matter to them, including how to articulate and deliver a compelling argument in favour of or against it.
After each team was scored for their performances, The Portsmouth Academy secured a top two finish, giving our team a chance to secure victory against The Petersfield School in the final.
It was a closely contested battle on whether artificial intelligence tools should be banned from the classroom, with the judge crowning us as the winners, due to the delivery of our opening and closing statements.
Many of the team had never spoken in front of a live audience before, which pushed them out of their comfort zone to grow and develop.
Speaking about their experience taking part in The Big Debate, Dara was grateful for the opportunity to meet with other schools, while Kayla said it was ‘one of the best experiences of my life’.
Our students didn’t just have to present their arguments to the opposing team and the judge, as over 70 people were in the room watching the action unfold.
Our Reading Champion, Ms Carter, supporting the students throughout The Big Debate. She felt extremely proud to see their confidence and hard work recognised.
"It's been a real pleasure to work with these students and for them to win the competition is a fantastic celebration of student voice.
“They showed courage, confidence and resilience to prepare and deliver strong arguments around important issues which they feel so passionately about.
"They'll take so much more from this experience than winning; it will give them the self-belief they need so they can be their best self at school and beyond".
At The Portsmouth Academy, extra-curricular opportunities are fundamental in helping our students become active citizens.
Discover how students use their voice at our Open Event on Thursday 1st October 2026, from 6pm-8pm.

June 16, 2026 07:28am
A Year 7 pupil from The Portsmouth Academy has been crowned the winner of our Planet Protectors creative writing competition.
Earlier this year, the Thinking Schools Academy Trust launched Planet Protectors in schools; a week-long celebration of how we can all work together to look after the environment.
Throughout the week, staff and students engaged with tailored activities to support with learning practical ways to reduce their environmental impact.
To support this, we challenged students across The Portsmouth Academy to write a poem about why it’s so important to protect our planet, and what they can do to help. This led to seven pupils across multiple year groups becoming our finalists, before a mystery judge determined the winner.
That mystery judge was Mark Waldron, Editor in Chief from The News, Portsmouth, who determined Diana, from Year 7, should take the crown with her poem ‘The Ocean’s Cry’. Her poem impressed with its vivid imagery around protecting our seas and marine life; something so important in a coastal city.
A special mention also goes to Sugoud and Yasna, also from Year 7, whose poem ‘The Ghost in the Cup’, was highly commended by Mark. Diana was ‘shocked’ to find out she was the overall winner, finishing above some strong poems written by her peers.
"I was trying really hard and it felt good because my work paid off. Writing (the poem) was time consuming but I’m glad because it raises awareness about plastic pollution”.
Mark recognised Planet Protectors as a ‘brilliant initiative’ which gets students at our school, and others across the trust, engaged with environmental issues.
“I was delighted to award the certificates and prizes to these wonderful students here at The Portsmouth Academy.
“Their creative talent to produce such impactful pieces of work is truly remarkable and they should feel so proud of themselves.
"Our environment and planet are so precious, and Planet Protectors is a brilliant initiative to get students actively engaged with a topic so important in today's world".
Planet Protectors isn’t just for its dedicated week, it’s a year-long trust-wide focus about showing how young people can positively change their future.
At The Portsmouth Academy, we’re proud to give pupils just like Diana, Sugoud and Yasna the opportunity to showcase their talent, while also having a bigger impact for their community.
Mrs S. Dedman, Principal at The Portsmouth Academy, praised the engagement from pupils across our school with the competition, and how those who received this special recognition lead the way as role models.
“It’s brilliant to see so much wonderful engagement with our creative writing initiative this year, and Diana, Sugoud and Yasna fully deserve their accolades.
“At The Portsmouth Academy, Planet Protectors was about more than just looking at environmental issues, it’s getting our pupils to understand the vital role they can play as active citizens in their local community and beyond.
“We’re proud to work with our students to help them discover how they can aspire and achieve beyond the curriculum, and poetry remains such a powerful way to strengthen their voice as young people”.
This competition wasn’t just about finding a winner; it highlighted how young voices at The Portsmouth Academy are developing creative talent and speaking up about issues important to them.
Is your child passionate about their local community and wider world? Come and discover The Portsmouth Academy at our Open Event on Thursday 1st October, from 6-8pm.

For some people, working while learning is the best next step for their education. Click here to explore the options available for students at The Portsmouth Academy.
There are a plethora of colleges available across Portsmouth and the surrounding areas for students at The Portsmouth Academy. We have listed those that may be of interest to pupils studying at our school.
Explore the variety of further education options available to pupils who leave The Portsmouth Academy. There is something for everyone, from T-levels and apprenticeships to vocational and technical qualifications.
By clicking through to this page, you will be presented with links that will allow you to download resources to support you with your post-secondary next steps.
Work experience opportunities are managed internally at The Portsmouth Academy. We have strong relationships with companies in the community and support our students with their placements.
An apprenticeship is an effective way to earn money while you are learn. They provide students with the skills and knowledge required for their career. Browse apprenticeships available on the Government website.
At The Portsmouth Academy, we believe careers education is a crucial part of a young person’s development.
By giving students impartial and independent access to information about a wide variety of possible career paths, we broaden their horizons and inspire them to achieve their goals and ambitions and to be the best that they can be.
We believe that good Careers Education, Information, Advice & Guidance (CEIAG) connects learning to the future. It motivates young people by giving them a clearer idea of the routes to jobs and careers that they will find engaging and rewarding. Good CEIAG widens pupils’ horizons, challenges stereotypes and raises aspirations. It provides pupils with the knowledge and skills necessary to make successful transitions to the next stage of their life. This supports social mobility by improving opportunities for all young people, especially those from disadvantaged backgrounds and those with special educational needs and disabilities.
The Portsmouth Academy is committed to providing all students in Years 7-11 with a stable programme of events and supporting activities to provide them with information and guidance about career opportunities and employment. The programme is designed to be progressive so that, each year, students will build and develop on the knowledge and skills that they have previously acquired. At The Portsmouth Academy our curriculum is designed to transform the life chances of all of our students, regardless of disadvantage or personal circumstances. We believe that the best way to transform life chances is to actively shape the minds, attitudes and habits of young people through a framework of cognitive education that enables them to become the master of their own destiny.
We are determined to prepare our students for the challenges they will face in 21st century society. We do this through teaching them to Aspire to greatness, to Achieve to the limits of their capability, and to show Respect in all that they do. We believe that a personalised approach based on these values will equip students with the tools they require to follow a path which will lead to success in whatever career they eventually choose
We provide ‘thinking toolkits’ to enable our students to approach learning in different ways. They encourage flexibility, creativity and critical thinking. Each student will develop habits of perseverance, open mindedness and teamwork, which will carry them beyond their time at school. Ofsted have reported on the links between being an outstanding school and a thinking school which you can read about here.
For any student who has additional and/or special educational needs we have an outstanding team to support them. Our experienced SENCo and their team of dedicated Student Engagement Workers will ensure that no child is left behind and all make exceptional progress. Equally we will ensure any student who exhibits exceptional talents will be nurtured to excel.
Home learning is an integral part of learning and the school experience. It is designed to encourage and extend learning beyond the classroom. Students are expected to take responsibility for their own learning at home and complete all activities in time and to a high standard.
There are 50 x 60 minute long lessons across a 2 week timetable. See learning day for info about how day is set out.

What is a Thinking School?
A Thinking School is unique in their focus to share with your child the tools to become a life-long learner, and to develop the best possible habits for success in life. It is an educational community which involves both students and staff learning how to think reflectively, critically and creatively.
We want every student in our schools to be inquisitive and confident in themselves. Our thinking toolkit is how we support them through this journey. These tools are used in tandem with an approach to teaching that instils a growth mindest and ‘can do’ attitude. Through their time in a Thinking School, students will develop the right habits to ensure they are successful throughout education and beyond.
More information on Thinking Schools, including our ‘Habits of Mind’ and ‘CoRT Tools’ can be found on our Trust website: https://www.tsatrust.org.uk/thinking-schools/
“Using all of the thinking tools, especially the thinking hats and thinking maps, has greatly aided me in my development and learning. Being on the Thinking Drive team is something that I am really proud of and gaining the advanced status is a real achievement for us all.”
-Sarah, Year 11
Thinking Tools and Strategies
Thinking Maps are eight graphic organisers that foster students’ abilities to see connections across their studies and encourage lifelong learning. Taken together they form a visual language of learning that is shared by staff and students.
Thinking Maps – A Guide
Widely used in business, Thinking Hats provide a practical method of directed cognition. Each of six distinct types of thinking are represented by a different coloured hat. When an individual is ‘wearing’ a specific hat they focus their thinking in the associated manner. Consequently the method helps people be more productive, focused, and mindfully involved.
Thinking Hats - A Guide
Thinkers’ Keys are a set of twenty different ways of approaching an issue or subject designed to engage and motivate learners in a range of thinking activities.
Thinking Keys- A Guide

The Bridge at The Portsmouth Academy is a specialist centre for children with complex Cognition and Learning difficulties aged between eleven and sixteen, who have an Education Health and Care Plan (EHCP).
What is an Inclusion Centre?
The Inclusion Centre is a resourced provision for students who have an Education and Health Care Plan (EHCP) or are currently undergoing assessment and are awarded placement by the Inclusion Support Panel (ISP), which is run by Portsmouth City Council’s Special Education Needs (SEN) Team. The students receive quality first teaching from the highly trained staff in The Bridge and are also expected to integrate into mainstream education for some learning. Students are offered support from the team to meet their specific needs in these mainstream lessons.
The Curriculum
Our curriculum centres on each student as an individual, looking at their starting points and next steps. We do not directly follow the national curriculum. Instead we use each student’s EHCP outcomes to plan a highly bespoke curriculum with a strong link to the Preparing for Adulthood outcomes. To complement lessons in The Bridge, students have the opportunity to participate in many local trips, work experience and visits to a local farm.
We work closely with the mainstream part of The Portsmouth Academy to ensure that there are meaningful opportunities for children to integrate and learn where appropriate. Where appropriate, we offer a ‘shadow curriculum’ which mirrors main school topics or units of learning but is adapted to best suit the needs of the students we support. However, these topics are a vehicle for individualising learning for students within the inclusion centre; as their learning will be highly personalised.
To ensure that our curriculum is student-centred, we work with a range of other professionals, including speech and language therapists, educational psychologists, physiotherapists, and occupational therapists, to ensure that each child’s holistic needs are being met as part of our curriculum.
Students will have the opportunity to gain a range of qualifications bespoke to them including Entry Level Certificates in Maths, English, Science and Digital skills. BTEC awards in Land Based studies, Personal Growth and Wellbeing and Home Cooking. Where appropriate students can also work towards Level 1 and GCSE’s in a range of subjects too.
Staffing
The Bridge Inclusion Centre currently has four class teachers, two HLTAs and four student engagement workers, led and managed by our Head of Inclusive Provision.
Working with Parents and Carers
We aim to foster strong relationships and work closely with parents and carers. We have regular contact with parents and carers using whichever method is best – in person, via telephone, or via email so that parents are kept informed about their child’s progress. We invite parents and careers to attend Pupil Progress sessions, Meet the Tutor evenings and Annual Review meetings where we can share updates and discuss next steps together with the student.
